subtitulo: The green cross, the list taped to the closed door, and the number that works from any phone
cena: It is Sunday evening, the pharmacy in front of you is shut, and there is a printed sheet taped inside the glass.
frasePiso: Name the symptom, name where it hurts, and let the pharmacist choose. The closed door still tells you where the open one is.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: 112 is the single European emergency number and works from any phone in Italy, including with no credit and, in most cases, with no SIM. Pharmacies operate a rota system: a closed pharmacy is required to display the farmacie di turno list showing which nearby pharmacy is on duty and when, and the same rotas are published by local health authorities.
fatosDatados.fonte: Commissione Europea — «112: il numero unico di emergenza europeo»; Federfarma — servizio di turno e reperibilità

steps.pt: This is the one part of the module that is purely defensive. It exists so that a bad night is short instead of long.
The green cross is the pharmacy. Inside, name the symptom — you are not expected to name the medicine.

steps.es: Ho mal di testa da ieri.
steps.pinyin: oh mal dee TES-ta da ee-EH-ri
steps.pt: I've had a headache since yesterday.
steps.tts: Ho mal di testa da ieri.

steps.promptPt: Say what hurts and since when. Two facts, no story. Speak now.
steps.es: Ho mal di testa da ieri.
steps.pinyin: oh mal dee TES-ta da ee-EH-ri
steps.pt: I've had a headache since yesterday.

steps.es: Prende altri farmaci? È allergico a qualcosa?
steps.pt: Are you taking other medication? Are you allergic to anything?
steps.tts: Prende altri farmaci? È allergico a qualcosa?
steps.acao: Answer both questions before they ask twice.

steps.pt: Mal di, plus the body part. Mal di testa, mal di gola, mal di stomaco, mal di denti. One pattern, four bad nights.

steps.promptPt: Same pattern, different body part: your throat. Speak now.
You cannot take one common ingredient. Subtract it, using the frame from B12. Speak now.
Ask whether it needs a prescription before they go and look. Speak now.

steps.pt: If the pharmacy is closed, read the door. The list taped inside says which one nearby is on duty tonight.

steps.es: Farmacie di turno: via Garibaldi dodici, aperta fino alle otto.
steps.pt: Duty pharmacies: via Garibaldi twelve, open until eight.
steps.tts: Farmacie di turno: via Garibaldi dodici, aperta fino alle otto.

steps.promptPt: Ask a passer-by which pharmacy is on duty. Speak now.
steps.es: C'è una farmacia di turno qui vicino?
steps.pinyin: cheh OO-na far-ma-CHEE-a dee TOOR-no kwee vee-CHEE-no
steps.pt: Is there a duty pharmacy near here?
steps.tts: C'è una farmacia di turno qui vicino?

steps.pt: For an emergency, one number: one-one-two. It works from any phone in Italy, with no credit and usually with no SIM.

steps.promptPt: Someone needs help now. Ask for an ambulance. Speak now.
On the phone to one-one-two, say where you are before anything else. Speak now.
steps.es: Sono in via Garibaldi, davanti alla farmacia.
steps.pinyin: SO-no een VEE-a ga-ree-BAL-dee, da-VAN-tee AL-la far-ma-CHEE-a
steps.pt: I'm on via Garibaldi, in front of the pharmacy.
steps.tts: Sono in via Garibaldi, davanti alla farmacia.

steps.promptPt: Ask where the emergency department is, using the frame from B07. Speak now.

steps.es: Ho mal di testa da ieri. C'è qualcosa senza aspirina? Dov'è il pronto soccorso?
steps.pinyin: oh mal dee TES-ta da ee-EH-ri. cheh kwal-KO-za SEN-tsa as-pee-REE-na. do-VEH eel PRON-to sok-KOR-so
steps.pt: Shadow the escalation: symptom, restriction, emergency.
steps.tts: Ho mal di testa da ieri. C'è qualcosa senza aspirina? Dov'è il pronto soccorso?

steps.pt: B17 done. Mal di plus the body part, the duty list on the closed door, one-one-two, and pronto soccorso.

aprofundar.titulo: The short version of a bad night

secoes.titulo: Mal di plus the body part
secoes.corpo: Testa, gola, stomaco, denti, schiena. You describe, the pharmacist prescribes — naming a symptom is more useful than guessing at a brand that may not exist here.

secoes.titulo: The Italian pharmacist is a first stop
secoes.corpo: Pharmacies handle a lot of what would be a clinic visit elsewhere, and they will tell you plainly when something needs a doctor instead. Going there first is the normal path, not a shortcut.

secoes.titulo: The closed door is still information
secoes.corpo: The rota list taped inside the glass names the pharmacy on duty and its hours. It is the single most useful thing about arriving at a shut pharmacy, and most visitors walk away without reading it.

secoes.titulo: 112, and the card you already have
secoes.corpo: 112 reaches emergency services from any phone. If you hold a European Health Insurance Card, or the UK equivalent, carry it — it covers state-provided necessary care on the same terms as a resident, and it is not a substitute for travel insurance.

permissao: You are allowed to go to a pharmacy for something small. Italian pharmacists deal with exactly this all day and will send you to a doctor if it warrants one — you do not have to decide in advance whether your problem is serious enough to be worth their time.
espelho: Anyone who has waited out an illness abroad because sorting out care felt harder than being unwell knows what this part is for. The calculation is the same at home; travel just adds a language to the excuse.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You arrive at a pharmacy on a Sunday evening and it is shut, with a printed sheet taped inside the glass.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: Everything is closed until Monday and I will have to wait it out.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Italian pharmacies run a duty rota, and a closed pharmacy is required to display the farmacie di turno list showing which one nearby is open and until when. The sheet in the window is the answer, not a notice about the closure.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Read the list for the nearest address and its hours, or ask a passer-by c'è una farmacia di turno qui vicino?
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: A bad night gets solved in twenty minutes instead of lasting until the next morning.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not a route for anything urgent — chest pain, breathing difficulty, a serious injury or a severe allergic reaction is 112 and pronto soccorso, not a pharmacy across town.
